q: 1. Who is recognized as the 'Father of SAARC' for mooting the concept of regional cooperation?
explain: Ziaur Rahman mooted the regional cooperation concept in 1980 and is historically recognized as the Father of SAARC. King Birendra hosted and inaugurated the Secretariat in Kathmandu; Rajiv Gandhi was a signatory for India; Jigme Singye Wangchuck was the signatory for Bhutan.

q: 2. The official SAARC Logo was designed by which Nepalese artist?
explain: The logo, featuring two hands and seven peace doves, was designed by Shailendra Maharjan, a famous artist from Nepal. Yadav Kant Silwal was Nepal's first Secretary-General, Mahesh Acharya signed the SAPTA agreement for Nepal, and Arjun Bahadur Thapa was Nepal's second Secretary-General.

q: 3. What is the official working language of SAARC?
explain: English is the official working and administrative language of the SAARC Secretariat and all intergovernmental activities. Hindi, Nepali, and Bengali represent national languages of member countries but are not the official administrative language of SAARC.

q: 4. In which month and year was the first SAARC Summit held?
explain: The 1st Summit took place on December 7-8, 1985, in Dhaka. November 1980 is when Ziaur Rahman formally mooted the concept; April 1981 was the Foreign Secretaries meeting in Colombo; August 1983 was the Foreign Ministers meeting in New Delhi.

q: 5. In which city did the Foreign Secretaries first meet in April 1981 to consult on South Asian cooperation?
explain: The Foreign Secretaries met in Colombo, Sri Lanka, in April 1981 to draft the initial areas of cooperation. New Delhi, Dhaka, and Kathmandu hosted later consultative or summit meetings.

q: 6. Which three SAARC member states are landlocked nations?
explain: These three are the only landlocked nations in the regional block. The other options are incorrect as they include coastal nations like Pakistan, Maldives, or Bangladesh.

q: 7. Which is the largest SAARC country by geographical area?
explain: India is the largest country with an area of 3.287 million sq km. Pakistan is the second largest; Afghanistan and Bangladesh are smaller by area rank.

q: 8. The national animal of Bhutan is the:
explain: The Takin (Budorcas taxicolor) is the national animal of Bhutan. Bengal Tiger is Bangladesh's national animal, Markhor is Pakistan's, and Lion is Sri Lanka's.

q: 9. Which SAARC country has the Markhor as its national animal?
explain: The Markhor is the national animal of Pakistan. Afghanistan has sheep, and India has the tiger.

q: 10. Which Article of the SAARC Charter outlines the eight core objectives of the Association?
explain: Article I defines the eight core objectives of the Association. Article II defines principles, Article III defines summits, and Article IV defines the Council of Ministers.

q: 11. Which Article of the SAARC Charter details the three operational principles of cooperation?
explain: Article II defines the three operational principles of cooperation. Article V governs the Standing Committee; Article VIII governs the Secretariat.

q: 12. Technical Committees of SAARC are governed under which Article of the Charter?
explain: Technical Committees comprising specialists are established and regulated under Article VI. Article VII governs Action Committees.

q: 13. Which Article of the SAARC Charter governs the establishment and role of the permanent Secretariat?
explain: Article VIII establishes the administrative Secretariat and governs the role of the Secretary-General. Articles VII and IX cover other details.

q: 14. General Provisions of the SAARC Charter are outlined in which Article?
explain: Article X contains the General Provisions, including consensus rules and bilateral exclusion. Articles IV and IX cover ministers and finance.

q: 15. Which of the following is an operational principle of SAARC under Article II?
options: Bilateral disputes shall be resolved by a majority vote
Cooperation shall substitute bilateral and multilateral cooperation
Cooperation shall be based on respect for sovereign equality and territorial integrity
Working language shall rotate among the member capitals
explain: This is the first principle under Article II. Bilateral disputes are excluded from the Charter; cooperation complements, not substitutes, bilateral frameworks.

q: 16. Who was the first person from Nepal to serve as the Secretary-General of SAARC?
explain: Yadav Kant Silwal was the first person from Nepal, serving as the 4th SG (1994-1995). Arjun Bahadur Thapa was the second person from Nepal.

q: 17. Who was the second person from Nepal to serve as the Secretary-General of SAARC?
explain: Arjun Bahadur Thapa was the second person from Nepal, serving as the 12th SG (2014-2017). Yadav Kant Silwal was the first; Dr. Bhesh Bahadur Thapa was a signatory to SAFTA.

q: 18. Which country did the first female Secretary-General of SAARC, Fathimath Dhiyana Saeed, represent?
explain: Fathimath Dhiyana Saeed represented the Maldives. The other options are other member nations.

q: 19. Who is the current Secretary-General of SAARC, assuming office on March 4, 2023?
explain: Golam Sarwar assumed office on March 4, 2023, as the 15th Secretary-General. The other options represent past Secretaries-General.

q: 20. What is the voluntary budget contribution share of Nepal in SAARC?
explain: Nepal pays a 10.72% share. 30.32% is India's, 22.52% is Pakistan's, and 5.00% is Bhutan's/Maldives'/Afghanistan's share.

q: 21. How many SAARC summits have been successfully hosted in Kathmandu, Nepal to date?
explain: Kathmandu, Nepal, has hosted four summits successfully (3rd, 11th, 18th, and 21st). Three excludes the 2023 21st Summit.

q: 22. Which Nepalese delegate participated on behalf of Nepal in the First SAARC Summit in 1985?
explain: King Birendra represented Nepal at the 1st Summit in 1985. King Gyanendra represented Nepal in 2005; the others represented Nepal in later years as Prime Ministers.

q: 23. Who represented Nepal as the Head of State during the 13th SAARC Summit in Dhaka in November 2005?
explain: King Gyanendra represented Nepal at the 13th Summit in Dhaka. King Birendra attended the first four summits; Koirala and Koirala were Heads of Government.

q: 24. Which Prime Minister represented Nepal at the 18th SAARC Summit in Kathmandu in November 2014?
explain: PM Sushil Koirala represented Nepal at the 18th Summit in Kathmandu in November 2014. The other options represented Nepal at other summits.

q: 25. Who represented Nepal at the 17th SAARC Summit in Addu City, Maldives (2011)?
explain: PM Dr. Baburam Bhattarai represented Nepal at the 17th Summit in Addu City, Maldives (2011). The other options are other Prime Ministers.

q: 26. Who signed the SAPTA Charter on behalf of the Government of Nepal?
explain: Finance Minister Mahesh Acharya signed SAPTA on behalf of Nepal. Dr. Bhesh Bahadur Thapa signed SAFTA; the others are Secretaries-General.

q: 27. At which Summit was the South Asian Free Trade Area (SAFTA) agreement reached and signed in January 2004?
explain: SAFTA was negotiated and signed on January 6, 2004, at the 12th Summit in Islamabad. The other options hosted different trade achievements.

q: 28. Before the 18th Summit, the SAARC regional centers were consolidated from eleven down to how many?
explain: Regional centers were consolidated from eleven down to five to reduce redundant expenses before the 18th Summit. The other options represent other administrative counts.

q: 29. With which SAARC country does Nepal conduct the least amount of trade?
explain: Maldives is the SAARC country with which Nepal conducts the least trade. The other options have higher recorded trade volumes.

q: 30. Who is the only person to be honored with the SAARC Award posthumously?
explain: Ziaur Rahman was posthumously honored as the only recipient of the SAARC Award. The other options are other historical figures of South Asia.

q: 31. When did SAARC Convention on preventing and combating Trafficking in women and children for prostitution signed in Kathmandu?
explain: The SAARC Convention on Preventing and Combating Trafficking in Women and Children for Prostitution was signed at the 11th SAARC Summit held in Kathmandu in 2002.

q: 32. Afghanistan participated as the 8th member of SAARC?
explain: Afghanistan formally joined SAARC as its eighth member during the 14th SAARC Summit held in New Delhi in 2007.

q: 33. Which SAARC summit envisioned the established of South Asian economic Union (SAEU)?
explain: The 18th SAARC Summit's declaration reaffirmed the long-term vision of moving towards a South Asian Economic Union (SAEU).

q: 34. When was South Asian Free Trade Area (SAFTA) come in force?
explain: Although SAFTA was signed in 2004, the agreement formally came into force on 1 January 2006.

q: 35. Where was the first summit of SAARC held in?
explain: The first SAARC Summit was held in Dhaka, Bangladesh in December 1985, where the SAARC Charter was adopted.

q: 36. Which SAARC Summit decided to establish the SAARC Development Fund (SDF) as a comprehensive funding mechanism with the provision of three windows (Social, Economic & Infrastructure)?
explain: The 13th SAARC Summit (Dhaka, 2005) decided to establish the SAARC Development Fund with Social, Economic, and Infrastructure windows.

q: 37. Currently, How many SAARC regional centers are in existence?
explain: SAARC originally had 11 regional centres, later consolidated and reduced to 5 to improve efficiency.

q: 38. Which SAARC Summit decided to reduce regional centre to from 11 to 5?
explain: The decision to consolidate SAARC's 11 regional centres into 5 was taken at the 18th SAARC Summit in Kathmandu (2014).

q: 39. Which country is not the founder member of the BIMSTEC?
explain: BIMSTEC was founded in 1997 by Bangladesh, India, Sri Lanka, and Thailand; Nepal joined later, in 2004, along with Bhutan.

q: 40. Where is BIMSTEC permanent secretariat located?
explain: The BIMSTEC Permanent Secretariat is located in Dhaka, Bangladesh.

q: 41. Which of the following is not the member state of BIMSTEC?
explain: BIMSTEC's seven members are Bangladesh, India, Myanmar, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Nepal, and Bhutan; Malaysia is not a member.

q: 42. When did Nepal formally get membership of BIMSTEC?
explain: Nepal formally became a member of BIMSTEC in February 2004.

q: 43. 6th BIMSTEC summit was concluded in Bangkok with signing and inception of ___ points.
explain: The 6th BIMSTEC Summit in Bangkok concluded with the signing/adoption of an 18-point declaration/outcome document.
